comments.author: JJJI_STUDIO
comments.body:
I've been developing **MARSTEAD**, a Mars colony survival and base-building game, with the help of GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, and Sonnet 5.5.

One interesting part of the development process was using **Sonnet 5.5 as a gameplay tester**.

I had AI agents test the game across multiple languages, and Sonnet kept detailed logs of its playthroughs, tracking resource shortages, colony events, and bugs.

For example, during one test, it discovered a colonist trapped inside the footprint of a solar panel and documented the issue.

I've attached screenshots of the multilingual testing sessions and Sonnet's playtest notes.

The **free demo is now available on Steam!**

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5129820/MARSTEAD/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5129820/MARSTEAD/)

replies.author: Apprehensive_Ad_7138
replies.body:
Oh, i didn't see the Steam page....if you mean to make this a commercial product, not to be harsh like the others but you will probably fail greatly.   
You are going against a GIANT game (which you know and love...i'm a huge fan too, got like 3k hours in it) with ten years of development and a cult-like fanbase. Whoever is into this kind of games will play Rimworld, buy Rimworld, or want something different than Rimworld.

How will you differentiate this?   
Rimworld was made as a simpler and more streamlined concept over games like Dwarf Fortress with a change of setting on top of it...so it had a place to be and a reason to exist...what will you do with this to give it a reason to exist?

You can take a look at how some people decided that another zombie game was useless, and just used Project Zomboid engine and framework to build a space station horror sim with plants invading everything...you keep the same kind of dynamics and interactions, but the game turns into something completely different.

comments.author: roach01gt
comments.body: What’s your main workflow between the three models?

replies.author: Novaleaf
replies.body: I also would love to hear your workflow details!

replies.author: JJJI_STUDIO
replies.body: Opus 5.5 designed the core game logic, while Astra mainly handled asset generation and verification. Sonnet 5.5 served as a highly cost-effective runner, spinning up multiple sub-agents to test different languages concurrently. Additionally, Astra and Opus cross-verified each other's outputs, effectively preventing overfitting issues.

replies.author: roach01gt
replies.body: I’ve generally settled into a similar workflow. Opus 5.5 is just all around a better game dev AI, while Astra is great for 3D assets and artwork generation. Sol 6.1 / Sonnet 5.5 as the coders. Letting them cross verify work. Depending on which you utilize the most, that’s who get the $100 sub. $20 to the other.
